blocks.text: Imagine a busy restaurant kitchen with multiple chefs. How do they decide who cooks which dish to ensure the fastest service? This is similar to how operating systems decide which process to run next using scheduling algorithms.

blocks.markdown: In operating systems, CPU scheduling is a fundamental task that determines which process in the ready queue will be allocated the CPU next. Efficient scheduling is crucial for system performance and responsiveness.

blocks.title: CPU Scheduling
blocks.text: CPU Scheduling is the process of determining which process in the ready queue is to be allocated the CPU next.

blocks.markdown: Let's explore some common scheduling algorithms: First-Come, First-Served (FCFS), Shortest Job First (SJF), Round Robin (RR), Priority Scheduling, and Multilevel Feedback Queues.

blocks.title: First-Come, First-Served (FCFS)
blocks.text: FCFS is the simplest scheduling algorithm where the process that arrives first gets executed first. It is non-preemptive.

blocks.title: Calculating Average Waiting Time for FCFS
blocks.prompt: Consider three processes P1, P2, and P3 with burst times of 4, 3, and 2 milliseconds, respectively, arriving in that order. Calculate the average waiting time using FCFS.

steps.text: List the processes in the order they arrive: P1, P2, P3.
Calculate waiting time for each process.

blocks.answer: The average waiting time for FCFS is 3.67 milliseconds.

blocks.title: Shortest Job First (SJF)
blocks.text: SJF selects the process with the smallest burst time from the ready queue. It can be preemptive or non-preemptive.

blocks.title: Comparing SJF and Round Robin
blocks.prompt: Given processes P1, P2, P3 with burst times 6, 8, 7 ms respectively, and a time quantum of 4 ms for Round Robin, compare the average turnaround time for SJF and RR.

steps.text: For SJF, order by burst time: P1, P3, P2.
Compute average turnaround time for SJF.
For RR, use time quantum 4 ms.
Compute average turnaround time for RR.

blocks.answer: The average turnaround time is 13.33 ms for SJF and 15.67 ms for RR.

blocks.title: Starvation in Scheduling
blocks.text: Starvation occurs when a process is perpetually denied necessary resources. This can happen in Priority Scheduling if low-priority processes never get CPU time.

blocks.markdown: To mitigate starvation, we use a technique called **ageing**, where the priority of a process increases the longer it waits.

points: FCFS is simple but can lead to long waiting times.
SJF minimizes average waiting time but may cause starvation.
Round Robin is fairer but can increase turnaround time.
Starvation can be mitigated using ageing.
